copy.failed: Copy failed. Select the text instead

date_picker.outside: That day is outside what can be chosen.
date_picker.not_a_day: That is not a day. Try {example} or 2026-10-05.

desktop_nav.pin_hint: Point at a page and press its pin to keep it here.

sidebar.label: Sidebar
sidebar.line: Every page in one quiet list down the side.

grouped.label: Grouped
grouped.line: The same list in named groups, so a page is found by where it lives.

rail.label: Rail that opens
rail.line: Icons until the pointer comes, then the whole sidebar over the page.

search.label: Search first
search.line: A large search above the pages, and rows a little larger.

dock.label: Dock
dock.line: The pages in a dock at the bottom; the status bar moves to the top.

command.label: Command bar
command.line: No list on screen: the page’s name at the top opens every page.

pinned.label: Pinned
pinned.line: The pages you pin on top, every page below in its group.

tiles.label: Coloured tiles
tiles.line: Each icon in a tile coloured by its group.

tabs.label: Tab bar
tabs.line: Four pages always at the bottom; More raises the rest.

peek.label: Peek
peek.line: A sheet that opens half way on the pages used most; drag it up for all of them.

full.label: Full screen
full.line: The whole screen becomes the menu, in large type.

arc.label: Thumb arc
arc.line: A corner button fans every page out around the thumb.

address.label: Address bar
address.line: A pill at the bottom names the page you are on and grows into the menu.

api.unreachable: Freightdock could not be reached. Is it running?

editor.env_help: NAME=value, a line each. Compose fills ${NAME} in the file with them; to hand them to a container as well, give its service env_file: .env.

setup.title: Welcome aboard
setup.sub: Make the first administrator to start.
setup.password_help: At least 12 characters. This account can do anything on every node of the cluster.
setup.token_help: On the server: docker exec freightdock freightdock setup-token. It is also in the log (docker logs freightdock), or it is FREIGHTDOCK_SETUP_TOKEN.

notfound.body: This address is not a page of Freightdock. It may have sunk.

login.turn_on_and_sign_in: Turn it on and sign in
login.required: Two-factor is required here. Set it up now to sign in.
login.type_code: Type the code your authenticator app shows for Freightdock.
login.or_directory: or with your password or directory password

two_factor.code_help: From your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.
two_factor.qr: QR code for your authenticator app
two_factor.scan: Scan it with an authenticator app (Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator, 1Password...). If it cannot scan, type this key into it:
two_factor.recovery_keep: Keep them somewhere safe, apart from your phone. Each one signs you in once in place of a code. Freightdock keeps only their hashes and cannot show them again.

registries.kept: Kept. Type a new one to change it.

users.password_help: At least 12 characters. They can change it in Account.
users.not_yourself: You cannot take this away from yourself.
users.admin_help: Everything, everywhere. Anybody else reads the cluster and changes nothing.
users.new_password_help: At least 12 characters. Their sessions end and their API tokens are revoked.
users.disable_body: They are signed out at once and cannot sign in, here or through SSO, until enabled again.
users.reset_totp_body: Their authenticator and recovery codes stop working. They sign in with the password alone, or set up a new authenticator at their next sign-in if two-factor is required.
users.remove_body: Their sessions, API tokens, roles and team places go with them.
users.users_sub: Who may sign in. An administrator changes the cluster; a user reads it.
users.no_teams_text: Put people who belong together in a team; a sign-in provider can fill teams from its groups.
users.remove_team_body: Its members stay; only the team goes.
users.sub: Who may sign in, and the teams they are in.

activity.empty_text: What people do in Freightdock shows here.
activity.sub: Who did what, and from where.

signins.nothing_text: Nobody signed in or out that way yet.
signins.sub: Who came in, how and from where.

account.copy_now: Copy it now: Freightdock keeps only a hash of it and cannot show it again. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
account.read_only_note: This token is read-only: whoever holds it can look, but every change it tries is refused.
account.ca_intro: Freightdock made its own HTTPS certificate, signed by a certificate authority of its own that lives in its data folder. Trust that CA once and every tool checks Freightdock’s certificate as it should, with no warning to click through.
account.whole_machine: Trust it on the whole machine, or in a browser
account.browsers: Chrome, Edge and Safari use the machine’s; Firefox has its own, under Settings, Privacy & Security, Certificates, View Certificates, Authorities, Import (or set security.enterprise_roots.enabled). Trusting it means trusting whatever this Freightdock signs, so keep its data folder to yourself.
account.token_name_help: What it is for, so you know which to revoke.
account.read_only_help: It may look at everything you may, and change nothing.
account.revoke_body: Whatever uses it is refused from now on.
account.tokens_sub: For scripts. A token acts as you; the activity log says which one made a change.
account.new_one_help: At least 12 characters. You stay signed in here; everywhere else you are signed out, and your API tokens are revoked.
account.sso_sub: Sign in to this account through a provider as well as with its password. An account is linked to one provider.
account.linked: Linked: the provider signs you in to this account from now on.
account.via_provider: You sign in through a provider, whose own two-factor applies.
account.required_next: Two-factor is required here: you will be asked to set it up at your next sign-in.
account.totp_intro: After your password, a six-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone. A password that leaks is then not enough.
account.few_codes: Few recovery codes left: make new ones.
account.old_stop: The ones you have stop working.
account.password_alone: Your password alone signs you in again.
account.two_factor_sub: A code from your phone after your password.
account.sub: Who you are signed in as, your password, two-factor, and your API tokens.
account.language_sub: The language Freightdock speaks in this browser. What the server says when something fails stays in English.
account.bad_redirect: The sign-in provider gave an address Freightdock will not follow.
account.linked_to: Linked: {name} signs you in to this account from now on.
account.signs_in_ldap: Signs in with a password checked by {name}
account.reads_the_cluster: A user: you read the cluster; an administrator changes it
account.certificate_sub: The authority that signed it, to trust once on each machine.
account.no_ca: Freightdock serves a certificate somebody gave it here, so there is nothing of Freightdock’s to trust.
account.signs_in_with_value: An API token, as Authorization: Bearer
account.connect_claude: Connect Claude Code to Freightdock with it:
account.mcp_off: The MCP server is turned off in this Freightdock: an administrator turns it on in Settings, under AI agents (MCP).
account.make_above: Make a token above, then run this with it in place of <token>:
account.agent_may: The agent may do what you may, or only look with a read-only token; every change it makes is in the activity log under the token’s name.
account.connect_agent_sub: Freightdock is an MCP server: an agent such as Claude Code can look at the cluster's nodes, stacks and events, deploy, start and stop stacks and read a container's logs through it, as you.
account.node_tool: Claude Code, and any Node tool

settings.defaults: Every choice at its default: FinUI as it ships.
settings.saved_everybody: Saved. Everybody sees it on their next page.
settings.appearance_sub: How Freightdock looks, for everybody on it
settings.preset_help: A code made at FinUI create: colours, corners, density and more. Paste the code, or the address or install line that holds it.
settings.sub: How Freightdock looks, and how it lets people in.

mcp_off_body.one: Every AI agent that uses it is refused from now on ({count} active token), until it is turned on again. The tokens stay good for the API.
mcp_off_body.other: Every AI agent that uses it is refused from now on ({count} active tokens), until it is turned on again. The tokens stay good for the API.

settings.revoke_body: Whatever uses it is refused from now on. They can make a new one in Account.
settings.no_tokens_text: Each person makes their own in Account.
settings.mcp_sub: Freightdock as an MCP server, for Claude Code and other agents
settings.mcp_help: Let AI agents in at /mcp with an API token, for the whole of this Freightdock. Off, /mcp refuses everybody; the tokens still work for the API.
settings.connect_claude: Connect Claude Code with a token in place of <token>:
settings.own_token: Make your own token in Account
settings.each_person: Each person makes theirs there; a token acts as its owner.

signin_settings.google_help: APIs & Services, Credentials: make an OAuth client ID of the kind Web application, with this as an authorized redirect URI. Google sends no groups: name the e-mail domains that may come in.
signin_settings.entra_help: App registrations, New registration: a Web redirect URI of this, then a client secret under Certificates & secrets. Put your tenant ID in the issuer. For groups, add the groups claim under Token configuration; Entra sends their object IDs, which are what the group lists below take.
signin_settings.github_help: Settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps (an organization’s, or yours): New OAuth App with this as the callback URL. The groups are your organizations (my-org) and teams (my-org/admins); the organization must allow the app (third-party access).
signin_settings.ldap_help: People sign in with their directory name and password in the usual form. Freightdock searches as the service account (read only is enough), then checks the password by binding as the person.
signin_settings.authentik_help: Make an OAuth2/OpenID provider, Confidential, with this redirect URI set to strict and only the authorization code and refresh token grants. Make an application for it, and bind it to the groups that may come in. The issuer is then https://<authentik>/application/o/<slug>/.
signin_settings.id_help: In its addresses: a to z, 0 to 9 and -. It cannot be changed later.
signin_settings.on_ldap: Check passwords typed in the sign-in form against this directory too.
signin_settings.on_oidc: Show its button on the sign-in page.
signin_settings.label_ldap: As the activity and auth logs name it.
signin_settings.label_oidc: The button reads Sign in with this.
signin_settings.github_address_help: https://github.com, or your GitHub Enterprise server.
signin_settings.issuer_help: The provider’s OpenID configuration URL without /.well-known/openid-configuration.
signin_settings.name_claim_help: The claim a person’s Freightdock name is taken from.
signin_settings.group_filter_help: {dn} is the person’s DN, {username} the name typed; both escaped. Active Directory’s member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:= follows nested groups.
signin_settings.starttls_help: For an ldap:// address: TLS before anything is sent.
signin_settings.allow_plain_help: No TLS at all: every password crosses the network as typed. Only on a network you trust; the activity log notes it.
signin_settings.ca_help: PEM. Trust this CA for the directory’s certificate instead of the system’s.
signin_settings.bind_password_help: Kept sealed; never shown again. Changing the address asks for it again.
signin_settings.user_filter_help: {username} is the name typed, escaped so it cannot change the filter.
signin_settings.id_attr_help: What a person is kept by when their name or place changes: entryUUID, or objectGUID in Active Directory.
signin_settings.admin_groups_github: Organizations or teams (org/team) whose members are administrators.
signin_settings.admin_groups_help: Members of any of these are administrators, set again at every sign-in. With none, a sign-in never changes anybody’s role.
signin_settings.user_groups_help: Members of any of these may sign in as users, who read the cluster. With both lists empty, everybody the provider lets through may.
signin_settings.domains_help: When any: only a person whose verified e-mail address is at one of these comes in.
signin_settings.link: Sign in to the local account with the same name
signin_settings.link_help: A person’s first sign-in lands in the local account of their name, if no one is linked to it yet. Off if people choose their own names there.
signin_settings.teams_on_help: At every sign-in, put people in the teams their groups map to, and out of the ones this provider put them in that they no longer map to. Teams given by hand stay.
signin_settings.teams_make: Make teams that are not there
signin_settings.teams_make_help: Otherwise a rule waits until an administrator makes its team.
signin_settings.team_rules_help: One a line: a group, -> and a team. A group between slashes is a regular expression whose captures the team may use ($1).
signin_settings.test_user_help: A name to look up; with a password, it is checked too.
signin_settings.not_found: Not found (or found more than once)
signin_settings.remove_body: Its button goes, and nobody signs in through it any more. Its people keep their accounts; those with no password can only come in another way.
signin_settings.none_yet: None yet. Passwords are the only way in.
signin_settings.providers_sub: Single sign-on and directories, besides the local passwords, which always keep working.

without.one: {count} person signs in with a password and no second factor yet; they set one up at their next sign-in.
without.other: {count} people sign in with a password and no second factor yet; each sets one up at their next sign-in.

signin_settings.tf_optional: Two-factor is up to each person.
signin_settings.tf_sub: A code from an authenticator app after the password: local accounts and directories. Single sign-on has its provider’s own.
signin_settings.required_all_help: Every sign-in with a password asks for a code; somebody without an authenticator sets one up then. An administrator can reset a lost one under Users.

changelog.sub: What changed in Freightdock, newest first.

cluster.sub: The Freightdock cluster this Freightdock is the UI of.
cluster.not_connected_text: Set FREIGHTDOCK_CLUSTER_API to a manager's admin API to show its cluster here.
cluster.no_nodes_text: Add a node to run workloads on it.
cluster.workload_help: The name the cluster knows this container by.
cluster.remove_body: Its certificate opens nothing more and its stream is cut. To come back it needs a new join token.
cluster.worker_token_text: Put this in /etc/freightdock/worker.env on the new node, with FREIGHTDOCK_MANAGERS set to this manager.
cluster.manager_token_text: Put this in /etc/freightdock/manager.env on the new manager, with FREIGHTDOCK_MANAGER_JOIN set to this manager.
cluster.token_once: It works once and is not shown again.
cluster.labels_help: One key=value a line. They go over the worker's own labels of the same key, and stacks place their workloads by them (node.labels.<key> in deploy.placement).
cluster.authorize_body: It came back fenced and runs no managed workload until it is authorized. Authorize it only when nothing it ran has been started elsewhere in the meantime.
cluster.no_worker: No worker heard on this host
cluster.floating_sub: Floating addresses of your LAN. A pool address answers only what a stack exposes on it (set on the Cluster stacks page), on any port, whichever worker runs the service; each worker can take an address over if one fails.
cluster.floating_none_text: Every published port answers on every worker's own address. Add an address of your LAN to have one that stays when a worker fails.
cluster.floating_add_help: One unused IPv4 address of the workers' LAN, or a range of them: 192.0.2.10-20 or 192.0.2.8/29 (at most 1024). Outside the cluster's own internal range. An address is used on the LAN only once a stack exposes on it.
cluster.name_help: Shown at the top of the dashboard and this page. Leave it empty to take the name away.
cluster.floating_standby_title: No stack exposes on this address, so no worker answers for it on the LAN yet. The worker named here takes it once one does.
cluster.floating_remove_body: Its holder lets it go, and nothing answers on it any more.
cluster.storage_none_text: Volumes stay on the worker that runs them, and their workloads wait for it if it fails. Add an NFS export or a shared directory to let them move.

storage_kind_title.nfs: The workers mount the export themselves, and unmount it when they fence.
storage_kind_title.path: A directory that is the same storage on every worker, shared outside Freightdock (a mount the host has, or a bind mount into a container).
storage_kind_title.cephfs: The workers mount the filesystem with the kernel client and its key; a fenced node's mounts are evicted by Ceph before its volumes move.

cluster.storage_in_use: A stack keeps a volume on it: remove the stack first.
cluster.storage_name_help: 1 to 40 of a-z, 0-9 and -. A Compose file names it.

storage_source_help.nfs: host:/export, as the workers reach it.
storage_source_help.path: An absolute directory, the same shared storage on every worker.
storage_source_help.cephfs: The monitors, comma separated, then : and the path in the filesystem (/ for all of it).

cluster.storage_compose_help: A stack keeps a named volume here from its Compose file: under volumes, give it x-freightdock with storage set to this name, and access: many if several workloads may write to it at once.
cluster.storage_remove_body: Nothing on it is deleted; the cluster stops using it.
cluster.storage_options_help_cephfs: name= the client the workers mount as (without client.), fs= the filesystem.
cluster.storage_secret_help: The key of the client named in the options, as ceph auth get-key prints it. Kept by the managers, never shown again.
cluster.storage_secret_set: Set. Leave empty to keep it.
cluster.storage_fence_client_help: Optional: a client allowed to evict others' mounts (mon 'allow r', mds 'allow *'), without client. Without it a fenced node's volumes wait for it to unmount by itself.
cluster.storage_fence_secret_help: Its key, kept and never shown like the mount key.

cluster_stacks.title: Cluster stacks
cluster_stacks.sub: Compose stacks the cluster runs, spread over its nodes and kept running by the managers.
cluster_stacks.none_text: Deploy one from a Compose file; the managers place its containers on the nodes.
cluster_stacks.recoveries_sub: Workloads the managers moved off a fenced node, or left there and why.
cluster_stacks.remove_body: Its containers are removed from every node. Named volumes stay.
cluster_stacks.name: Name
cluster_stacks.name_help: 1 to 40 of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit.
cluster_stacks.no_pool: The pool has no addresses yet: add one on the Cluster page first.
cluster_stacks.exposure_incomplete: Every exposure needs a container port, an address and a port.
cluster_stacks.reach_pool_help: An exposure on a pool address: answered on that address only.
cluster_stacks.reach_internal_help: Not published: other services of the stack reach it by name.
cluster_stacks.search: Search stacks, services, images, workers, addresses
cluster_stacks.none_match_text: Change the search or the filters above.
cluster_stacks.reach_asked_help: A port in the Compose file opens nothing by itself. Expose it on a pool address to reach it from outside the cluster.
cluster_stacks.waits_for: Waits for its old copy on {node} to stop

cluster_node.title: Node
cluster_node.sub: A node of the cluster: what it is, and what runs on it.
cluster_node.sub_named: Its hostname is {hostname}; the managers call it by this name too.
cluster_node.no_report_text: No manager has heard from this node's worker lately.
cluster_node.no_workloads: No stack has a workload placed on this node.
cluster_node.name: Name
cluster_node.name_help: Shown instead of the hostname, here and by the managers (as its name label). The node keeps its hostname. Empty gives the hostname back.

cluster_manager.title: Manager
cluster_manager.sub: A manager of the cluster: its place in Raft and the workers it hears.
cluster_manager.sub_named: Its address is {addr}; the name is Freightdock's only.
cluster_manager.gone_text: No manager of the cluster has this raft id.
cluster_manager.no_workers: No worker holds its stream with this manager.
cluster_manager.name_help: Shown in Freightdock instead of the address. The managers keep its raft id and address. Empty gives the address back.

network.title: Network
network.sub: Who talks to whom in the cluster, live: since the last heartbeat of each node.
network.map_sub: Point at a workload or a node to see only its lines; click to keep it. A line is as thick as its traffic and moves the way the connections went.
network.map_label: The cluster network with {n} lines of traffic
network.none_reporting_text: The workers read their traffic with conntrack; install it on them (install-node.sh does).
network.quiet: Nothing moved since the last heartbeat.

cluster_deploy.stopped_help: It is placed and kept, and nothing of it runs until you start it on the Stacks page.
cluster_deploy.title: New stack
cluster_deploy.sub: A Compose file, where it runs, and what of it is reached from outside the cluster. The managers check it as you write; nothing runs until you deploy.
cluster_deploy.compose_help: image, command, environment, labels, ports, volumes and deploy (replicas, placement, resources) are used; what is not supported yet is named below. Ports here open nothing by themselves: they are offered under Reached from outside. A named volume stays on its worker unless its x-freightdock names storage of the cluster's to keep it on.
cluster_deploy.where_sub: Its workloads are placed only on healthy workers, and moved off one that fails.
cluster_deploy.any_help: The managers place each workload on the least loaded healthy worker that meets its Compose constraints.
cluster_deploy.chosen_help: Only these workers run it. If none of them is healthy, its workloads wait for one.
cluster_deploy.stays: Its workloads stay where they run.
cluster_deploy.reach_sub: Only what is listed here with a pool address is reachable from outside the cluster.
cluster_deploy.reach_text: A pool address answers only the ports listed here, and follows the service to whichever worker runs it. Services of the stack reach each other by name inside the cluster and need nothing here. Set a row to Internal only to keep that port inside.
cluster_deploy.description_help: What the stack is for, shown on its card. At most 500 characters.
cluster_deploy.env_help: KEY=value lines. They fill the file's variables ($TAG and the other forms Compose has) and an environment name given with no value. Kept with the stack, shown only to administrators here.
cluster_deploy.selector_help: Only workers with these labels run it, comma separated: zone=a, disk!=hdd. When a worker's labels change, its workloads move to one that has them.
cluster_deploy.mode_sub: Over what the Compose file says for each service.

mode_help.file: Each service as its file says: it moves to another worker, unless its x-freightdock says ha: false.
mode_help.stateless: Every workload moves to a healthy worker at once. Named volumes stay on each worker: what was written there is not taken along.
mode_help.pinned: Every workload waits for its own worker to come back, with its data there. Nothing moves by itself.
mode_help.shared: Every workload moves, and its named volumes are kept on the cluster's storage, one writer at a time, so its data moves with it.

cluster_deploy.mode_no_storage: The cluster has no storage yet: add it on the Cluster page.
cluster_deploy.names_help: Container names, each its own in the cluster and a name for it inside the stack too. Left empty: the file's container_name, else stack-service-replica.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.sub: What the cluster works with and how it behaves. A change here is every manager's.
integrations.shares_sub: Shared storage the workers keep volumes on: an NFS export they mount, or a directory each one has.
integrations.fencing_sub: How a worker the cluster no longer hears is made sure to be off before its workloads run elsewhere.
integrations.no_provider_text: With no provider, a worker cut off stops its workloads by its own timers and the cluster waits them out. Proxmox powers a worker's guest off instead, and says so: faster, and proven.
integrations.proxmox_url_help: https:// and a node's address, port 8006 unless given.
integrations.proxmox_fingerprint_help: The API certificate's SHA-256. Read it, then compare it with the one on the Proxmox node's Certificates page.
integrations.proxmox_token_help: user@realm!tokenid=secret. Kept by the managers, never shown again.
integrations.proxmox_token_kept: {id} (kept; type a new one to replace it)
integrations.proxmox_rights: The token needs VM.PowerMgmt and VM.Audit on the workers' guests, and nothing more.
integrations.test_no_guests: No worker is fenced through Proxmox yet.
integrations.remove_body: Workers labelled for Proxmox cannot be fenced through it until it is set again.
integrations.pve_node_help: The node the guest runs on, as Proxmox names it.
integrations.vmid_help: The VM or container id, a number from 100.
integrations.by_help: Fenced by itself, the worker stops its workloads when it hears no manager. Through Proxmox or Redfish, the leader powers its guest or server off and waits until Proxmox or the BMC says it is off.
integrations.timings_sub: How nodes are watched and how long fencing and recovery take.
integrations.timings_note: Workers take new timers at once; nothing restarts.
integrations.manager_sub: What a manager needs before it can reach the cluster, so only its environment sets it.
integrations.manager_note: As the manager answering now has them. Change them in /etc/freightdock/manager.env on that manager.

help.suspect_ms: Unheard this long, a worker is suspect.
help.unreachable_ms: Unheard this long, it is unreachable and fencing starts.
help.fence_stop_s: A worker that hears no manager this long stops its workloads.
help.fence_storage_s: Then this long later it unmounts the shared storage.
help.fence_reboot_s: Then this long later it reboots if it could not stop them.
help.recovery_delay_s: How long a fenced worker's workloads wait before they run elsewhere.
help.fence: Off, an unheard worker is only unreachable: nothing moves.
help.auto_authorize: A worker that comes back fenced runs workloads again by itself; off, an administrator authorizes it.
help.backup_passphrase: What the scheduled backups are sealed with. None is written without it.
help.backup_every_h: Hours between each manager's backups; 0 writes none.
help.backup_keep: How many backups each manager keeps; the oldest go.
help.shells: An administrator may open a shell on a node, or in a container, from its page. Off, nobody can, from the UI or the API. A node's owner can still turn off its own host shell on the node.

integrations.backups_sub: The cluster's state (stacks, nodes, storage, settings, users) and its certificate authority, sealed with a passphrase.
integrations.backup_holds: A backup is the whole cluster
integrations.backup_holds_text: With its passphrase it holds every secret of the cluster, its CA's key among them. Keep the file and the passphrase apart.
integrations.passphrase_help: At least 12 characters. Without it the backup cannot be opened, by anybody.
integrations.passphrase_differs: The two are not the same.
integrations.passphrase_keep: The managers keep it to seal their scheduled backups; it is never shown again. Keep a copy of it apart from the backups.
integrations.passphrase_off_body: The passphrase is removed and the managers write no more backups. The ones already written stay.
integrations.stored_sub: The scheduled backups on the manager that answered; each manager keeps its own.
integrations.no_backups_text: Set a passphrase and the managers write them on their schedule.
integrations.restore_text: On a new manager, before its first start, run the line below with the backup's file and its passphrase; it then starts as the cluster it was, and the workers' certificates are still good.
integrations.registries_sub: A login per registry: the workers pull its images with it. The password is never shown again.
integrations.registry_help: As images name it: ghcr.io, registry.example:5000, or docker.io for Docker Hub.
integrations.registry_password_help: A token that only reads is enough, and safer.
integrations.registry_remove_body: Images from it are pulled without a login from then on; a private one fails unless the node has it.
integrations.notifications_sub: Where the cluster tells what happens to it. The leading manager tells each change once, the same news at most once in ten minutes.
integrations.no_channels_text: Nobody is told when a node goes down until one is added.
integrations.channel_remove_body: Nothing is told through it from then on.
integrations.channel_url_help: Freightdock POSTs a JSON body here, signed when it has a key.
integrations.channel_smtp_port_help: Left empty: 587 with STARTTLS, 465 with TLS, 25 with none.
integrations.channel_to_help: One address or several, separated by commas.
integrations.secret_webhook_help: Optional. The body's HMAC-SHA256 under it goes in X-Freightdock-Signature, as GitHub signs its hooks.
integrations.secret_ntfy_help: Optional: for a topic that is not open to all.
integrations.secret_gotify_help: The token of a Gotify application made for the cluster.
integrations.secret_email_help: With the user above, if the server asks for a login.

ev.node_awaiting: A node waits to be let back
ev.storage_back: A node's shared storage answers again

integrations.redfish_none: No BMC account yet. Bare-metal workers can be powered off through their BMC (iDRAC, iLO or any Redfish service) once one is set.
integrations.redfish_password_kept: (kept; type a new one to replace it)
integrations.redfish_password_help: Kept by the managers, never shown again.
integrations.redfish_rights: One account on every worker's BMC, with the right to reset the system (iDRAC: Operator) and nothing more.
integrations.redfish_no_nodes: No worker is fenced through Redfish yet.
integrations.test_failed_redfish: The BMCs could not be tried
integrations.testing_redfish: Asking the BMCs from a manager...
integrations.redfish_remove_body: Workers labelled for Redfish cannot be fenced through their BMC until it is set again.
integrations.bmc_host_help: The BMC's host or address, port 443 unless given.
integrations.bmc_fingerprint_help: The BMC certificate's SHA-256. Read it, then compare it with the one the BMC's own page shows.
integrations.bmc_system_help: Only when the BMC manages more than one system: its id under /redfish/v1/Systems.
integrations.proxmox_none: Not set up. Workers that are Proxmox guests can be powered off through its API once it is.
integrations.portainer_sub: Bring a Portainer's Compose stacks into the cluster. Freightdock only reads Portainer; nothing there changes.
integrations.portainer_none: Not connected. Give Portainer's address and an access token to see what it has.
integrations.portainer_token_kept: (kept; type a new one to replace it)
integrations.portainer_token_help: In Portainer: My account, Access tokens, Add access token. An administrator's, so every stack can be read. Kept sealed, never shown again.
integrations.portainer_ca_help: Only when Portainer has a certificate of its own making: paste it (PEM), and it is trusted as itself.
integrations.portainer_skip_help: Anybody between here and Portainer could read the token. Recorded in the activity log.
integrations.portainer_forget_body: Its token is removed. Stacks already brought in stay.
integrations.portainer_start: Start them in the cluster now
integrations.portainer_start_help: Off, they are made stopped: stop each in Portainer first, then start it on Cluster stacks, so it never runs twice.
integrations.portainer_from: From {url}, Portainer {version}. Ticked: what can come; the others say why not.

cluster_docker.title: Docker
cluster_docker.sub: This node's containers, images, volumes and networks, asked of its worker now. The cluster's own are changed through their stack.
cluster_docker.name: Name
cluster_docker.remove_container_body: The container goes, running or not, and what it kept outside its volumes with it.
cluster_docker.remove_image_body: Docker keeps an image a container uses, and says so.
cluster_docker.remove_volume_body: The volume and everything in it go. Docker keeps one a container uses.
cluster_docker.remove_network_body: Docker keeps a network a container is on.
cluster_docker.volumes_note: Volumes on the cluster's storage are mounted where their workload runs; the ones here are this node's own.
cluster_docker.pull_title: Pull an image onto this node
cluster_docker.pull_help: A name and tag, as docker pull takes it. A stack's images are pulled where its workloads run, without this.
cluster_docker.prune_body: Images without a tag that no container uses go.
cluster_docker.cut: Only the newest lines are shown: the rest is over a mebibyte.

ceph.title: Ceph
ceph.sub: Shared storage the cluster makes of its own nodes' disks: Ceph on the nodes chosen, its filesystem added as storage.
ceph.none_text: Pick the nodes and their empty disks, and the cluster sets up Ceph on them step by step. Three nodes or more keep it working when one fails.

kind.keys: Make the keys and the storage

ceph.done_text: Its filesystem is the storage {storage}, under Shared storage above.
ceph.clear_body: Only the record of it goes: Ceph stays on the nodes and its storage stays the cluster's.
ceph.looking: Asking each node for its disks…
ceph.no_nodes_text: Ceph is set up on nodes that are heard, not fenced, and run Docker.
ceph.no_disks: No disks of its own (a container sees none).
ceph.pick: Tick at least one empty disk.
ceph.picked_few: {n} node(s); {first} starts Ceph. With fewer than three, Ceph stops when one fails.
ceph.storage_help: The name stacks give in their Compose files, as for any storage.
ceph.fs_help: The CephFS made on the disks.
ceph.image_help: Optional: the image Ceph runs from. Empty is the release Freightdock is tried with.
ceph.erase_text: Ceph takes each disk whole. Only disks the node says are empty (no partitions, no filesystem, not mounted) can be ticked.
ceph.confirm_title: Set up Ceph on these disks?
ceph.confirm_body: Everything on {disks} is erased. This cannot be undone.
ceph.started: Ceph is being set up ({n} steps)
ceph.none_free: None of its {n} disks is free: {why}.

terminal.sub_host: A login shell as root on the node itself. What you type is not recorded; that you opened it is.
terminal.sub_container: bash, or sh where there is none, in the container. What you type is not recorded; that you opened it is.
terminal.failed: The shell could not be opened
